gallery.filename: 12 - Brisbane Powerhouse (4741179311).jpg
gallery.title: File:12 - Brisbane Powerhouse (4741179311).jpg
gallery.description: Brisbane Powerhouse, a world-class entertainment venue with cafes and restaurants, was once the New Farm Powerhouse, Brisbane’s first municipal power station which operated from 1928 to 1971. It was built by Brisbane City Council Tramways Department architect, Roy Rusden Ogg, and originally supplied electricity for the city’s tramway system. Some of the power station’s machinery has been retained, along with the graffiti on the walls from when the building lay derelict for many years.

gallery.filename: Altostratus undulatus New Farm Powerhouse theatre New Farm P1260778.jpg
gallery.title: File:Altostratus undulatus New Farm Powerhouse theatre New Farm P1260778.jpg
gallery.description:
Brisbane Powerhouse is an arts and cultural hub located in a former power station in the Brisbane suburb of New Farm, Queensland, Australia. The venue offers an array of performing arts, visual arts, festivals, and free community events.
The adaptation potential to reuse the existing structures without detracting from the cultural significance was recognised and architect Peter Roy was commissioned to create an arts venue from the site.
